campaigns.name: V2 SweepzKings
campaigns.takeaways:
*CTR of 3.2% indicates moderate engagement, but acquisition volume remains limited.

*Zero FTDs and revenue mean the campaign has not demonstrated downstream value.
campaigns.lessons:
Generating registrations is not enough if users do not progress through the funnel.

The current creative and audience combination has not demonstrated sufficient conversion quality.

More spend will not solve an unproven conversion funnel.
campaigns.improvements:
Test stronger acquisition messaging to improve CTR and registration volume.

Identify where users abandon the registration-to-FTD journey.

Keep spending controlled until downstream conversion is demonstrated.

campaigns.name: V1 Imperial Sweeps
campaigns.takeaways:
Achieved a 6.1% CTR, the highest among the Facebook campaigns.

Despite strong engagement and acquisition efficiency, generated zero FTDs and revenue.
campaigns.lessons:
The campaign attracts attention, but engagement has not translated into business value.

Low CPR can create a misleading impression of success when downstream conversions are absent.

The creative approach is worth testing further, but the audience quality remains unvalidated.
campaigns.improvements:
Preserve the high-performing creative elements while testing alternative conversion-focused messaging.

Analyze registration quality and identify barriers to FTD conversion.

Evaluate success against qualified users and revenue, not CTR alone.

campaigns.name: C4 Imperial Sweeps
campaigns.takeaways:
Delivered 31 registrations at a $3.55 CPR, the strongest acquisition efficiency across all six campaigns.

Generated 1 FTD and $140 revenue from $110 spend.

Reported ROI of +27.3%, but revenue still exceeded spend by only $30.
campaigns.lessons:
C4 is the strongest registration acquisition benchmark, but its downstream conversion rate remains low.

High registration volume does not automatically produce proportional revenue.

The campaign has demonstrated revenue potential, but not yet enough evidence for aggressive scaling.
campaigns.improvements:
Replicate the winning acquisition elements in controlled creative tests.

Improve the 3.2% S2P rate to increase the value generated from existing registrations.

Focus on improving revenue per registration before substantially increasing spend.

campaigns.name: C2 SweepzKings
campaigns.takeaways:
Generated 15 registrations at a $7.53 CPR, more than twice C4's acquisition cost.

Recorded a 2.1% CTR, indicating weaker engagement than the other Facebook campaigns.

Generated 1 FTD and $140 revenue against $113 spend, with a reported +23.9% ROI.
campaigns.lessons:
The campaign can generate downstream value, but its acquisition efficiency is weaker than C4.

Low CTR is a clear signal to investigate creative relevance and audience response.

One FTD is not sufficient evidence to establish consistent profitability.

What Can Be Improved
campaigns.improvements:
Test C4's stronger creative structure against C2's existing concepts.

Improve CTR to reduce inefficient traffic acquisition.

Optimize toward qualified registrations and repeatable FTD volume rather than simply increasing registrations.

campaigns.name: C3 Imperial Sweeps
campaigns.takeaways:
Generated only 2 registrations from $104 spend, resulting in a $52 CPR.

Achieved a 3.2% CTR but failed to convert traffic into meaningful registration volume.

Generated zero FTDs and revenue, resulting in a -100% reported ROI.
campaigns.lessons:
Traffic generation is not the primary problem to solve; post-click conversion requires investigation.

The campaign consumed almost half of Instagram's total spend while generating only 2 registrations.

The current audience and creative combination has not justified its investment.
campaigns.improvements:
Reassess audience quality and test alternative creative concepts.

Reduce or pause spend until conversion efficiency improves and the funnel is validated.

campaigns.name: C1 SweepzKings
campaigns.takeaways:
Generated 14 registrations at a $7.43 CPR, accounting for the majority of Instagram registrations.

Delivered 1 FTD and $140 revenue from $104 spend.

Reported a +34.6% ROI, the strongest reported ROI across the six campaigns.
campaigns.lessons:
C1 demonstrated that Instagram can generate downstream value when the campaign converts.

Its 7.1% S2P rate was stronger than C4 and C2, despite lower registration volume.

Revenue performance is encouraging, but its 1.5% CTR reveals an opportunity to acquire more efficiently.
campaigns.improvements:
Improve creative engagement to increase CTR without sacrificing registration quality.

Test variations of the current winning creative and audience combination.

Explore controlled budget increases only after confirming that FTD and revenue performance is repeatable.
